CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough for one week

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 74-year-old male who reports that his cough started approximately one week ago. He has been bringing up yellow sputum and reports feeling worse over the last two days. He denies fever but reports feeling warm. He denies chills but notes he feels a little achy at times. He denies shortness of breath. He reports nasal congestion with drainage down his throat and some pressure in his sinuses. No one else in his household is sick. Patient also reports that while coughing earlier today, he fell down approximately four to five stairs and twisted his right knee. He reports pain on the inside of his knee, particularly with palpation, and has a slight limp but is still able to walk. He denies feeling like the knee will give out. He has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for his cough and cold symptoms, which has helped a little bit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever. Denies chills. Reports feeling achy at times. Denies shortness of breath. Reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and sinus pressure. No other sick contacts in household.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 milligrams daily
Metformin 1000 milligrams twice daily
Over-the-counter Dayquil

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. Not a sports fan.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62 mmHg, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen saturation 97% on room air
Facial Exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses
Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of bilateral nasal turbinates with yellow discharge
Throat Exam: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space
Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy
Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough
Heart Exam: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation on right knee, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 milligrams twice daily to help with sputum expectoration. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; chest X-ray may be considered if worsening occurs to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right knee pain/Right medial collateral ligament strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 milligrams once daily. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises. Order right knee X-ray to rule out bony injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel.

4. Diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess need for metformin adjustment. Patient counseled on importance of monitoring sugar intake and diet to prevent complications such as kidney dysfunction and eye problems. Encouraged to report blood sugars through patient portal.
